## [2.49.68] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Add a design plan for the Player Simulacrum feature.** Doc-only. New plan at `docs/plans/player-simulacrum.md`: a private per-player tabletop where a player takes their character into a sandbox to test how abilities work, with the existing demo map + demo NPC templates available for placement. Concept came from the user's "let players test abilities without disrupting the table" use case. Plan covers four approach options (rejects three, recommends one), the data model (one `is_simulacrum` boolean + two provenance pointer columns on `Campaign`), the lifecycle (enter → clone → play → refresh / reset / delete), endpoint surface (5 new endpoints; every existing endpoint works unchanged because the sim is a real campaign), and 7-row "Interface changes — at a glance" summary table + 4 visual mockups. Includes file-path index for the implementation agent. The plan is surfaced through the wiki at `/wiki/doc/plan-player-simulacrum` in the same commit (per the v2.49.66 three-step checklist) — allowlist + landing-page table + on-disk README + per-slug harness smoke test. PATCH — additive doc + additive wiki entry + 1 additive harness test; no production code change.
**Description:** Five edits + one new file. **(1)** `docs/plans/player-simulacrum.md` (NEW, ~390 lines). Eight sections: Goal, Interface changes summary, Constraints, Approaches considered (A in-memory rejected · B forked-campaign chosen · C sandbox-mode rejected · D action-preview rejected), Chosen approach detailed design (data model + lifecycle diagram + cloning spec + endpoint signatures), Mockups (Enter button + persistent banner + Enemies palette tab + flow modals), Implementation phases (3 phases with LOC + test estimates), Open questions (7 items), Filed follow-ups, File-path index, Decision log. **(2)** `app/routes/wiki_routes.py::_DOC_ALLOWLIST` — new `plan-player-simulacrum` row. **(3)** `app/templates/wiki.html` — design-plans table row. **(4)** `docs/wiki/README.md` — design-plans table row. **(5)** `tests/harness/test_wiki.py` — new per-slug test + landing-page assertion. **(6)** `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog row; total 279 → 280.
**Description (cont):** Why "forked campaign per (character, user)" is the load-bearing decision. The alternatives all duplicate code. In-memory shadow state means every endpoint that mutates anything (attack / cast / use_feature / move / use_item — 12+ endpoints) needs a sim-mode branch and a parallel WS channel model. Sandbox-mode toggle on the character is the same trap with a different label. The chosen approach creates a NEW Campaign row + clones the character into it + reuses every existing endpoint because the auth model is already campaign-scoped. Result: ~600 server LOC for the entry / clone / refresh helpers + 5 new endpoints, vs. 1500+ for the alternatives. Plus persistence comes free (state survives container restart since the sim is real DB rows).
**Description (cont 2):** Why a separate Campaign row rather than an in-place sandbox flag on the source character. The campaign model is where the auth + WS + roll-log + battle state isolation already lives. Cloning into a new campaign borrows all of that. Putting the simulacrum "on" the existing character would require teaching every endpoint that "when in sandbox mode, spell slots / HP / buffs go to `_sandbox_slots`, `_sandbox_hp`, etc." — and the same for the roll log, the battle state, the buffs list. Massive code duplication for what the campaign model already provides for free.
**Description (cont 3):** Why one sim per (character, user) and not unlimited. A user could spawn 100 simulacrums of the same character to spam DB rows. The unique partial index `(simulacrum_source_character_id, gm_user_id) WHERE is_simulacrum=true` makes that impossible at the DB level. Players who want multiple simultaneous experiments can create multiple characters in their main campaign first (already allowed) and get one sim per character.
**Description (cont 4):** Why no GM peek in v1. Privacy is the load-bearing UX feature. If the GM can see what the player is testing, the player is back in the same "I don't want to embarrass myself" position the simulacrum exists to fix. A future "invite GM as member" path covers the explicit-consent case without baking peek into the auth model.
**Description (cont 5):** Why ALL three wiki-surfacing edits land in the same commit as the plan write. Closes the discovery gap that v2.49.59's ruler plan tripped (plan written + on disk but not surfaced through the wiki until v2.49.66 retro-fixed it). Future plan-write commits should follow the same pattern — plan + allowlist + landing-page + on-disk index + harness test in one atomic commit. This is exactly the rule the next commit (v2.49.69) codifies in CLAUDE.md.
**Description (cont 6):** Verification. Pre-commit: GET `/wiki/doc/plan-player-simulacrum` returned 404 (slug not in allowlist). Post-commit + rebuild: returns 200 + the rendered plan + the wiki nav. The new per-slug harness test passes; the landing-page test still passes with the new assertion. Full regression: 280 harness tests pass (was 279, +1 new wiki test). No production code touched.

### Added
- `docs/plans/player-simulacrum.md` — design plan for the per-player private testing sandbox.
- `app/routes/wiki_routes.py::_DOC_ALLOWLIST` — new `plan-player-simulacrum` entry.
- `app/templates/wiki.html` — new design-plans table row.
- `docs/wiki/README.md` — new design-plans table row.
- `tests/harness/test_wiki.py::test_wiki_doc_serves_simulacrum_plan` — per-slug smoke test.
- `tests/harness/test_wiki.py::test_wiki_home_renders` — added landing-page assertion for the new slug.
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog row; total 279 → 280.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Doc-only on the production side; new harness test is additive.
- **All four wiki-surfacing steps landed atomically.** First commit since v2.49.66's retro-fix to follow the full checklist on the plan-write commit itself.
- **Three-phase implementation roadmap.** Phase 1 (entry + character clone + banner) is shippable alone — players can already mess around with their cloned character. Phase 2 unlocks the Enemies palette. Phase 3 polishes (reset, cleanup, campaign-list grouping).

### Filed
- **Phase 1 implementation** — schema migration + `/enter` + `/refresh_character` endpoints + cloning helpers + sheet button + banner partial.
- **Phase 2 implementation** — Enemies palette tab + drag-to-place wiring + `GET /simulacrum/enemies` endpoint.
- **Phase 3 implementation** — `/reset_map` + `DELETE` cleanup + campaign-list grouping + switch-existing-sim modal.
- **GM peek toggle** — opt-in flag for GMs to view player sims (privacy-by-default in v1; this is the explicit-consent escape hatch).
- **Multi-character sims** — currently one sim per character; future could allow N characters in one sim for party-vs-party testing.

This is the first test to pin the "non-incapacitating condition buff" branch of the hook (Hold Person, Stunning Strike, and Sleep all test incapacitating buffs; the symmetric "this buff does NOT incapacitate" assertion was unpinned until now). Test-only; production code untouched. 3 new harness tests. PATCH.
**Description:** Two edits. **(1)** `tests/harness/test_use_open_hand_technique.py` — appended three PC tests + three small helpers (`_install_hex`, `_buff_keys`, `_pc_combatant`). All three share the same battle-seeding pattern as the existing NPC tests. `test_open_hand_prone_pc_installs_prone` retries up to 20 iterations on the DEX save (random); the other two are single-iteration (no save → deterministic install; push has a save but the assertion is "no buff installed regardless of outcome"). **(2)** `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — three new rows under `test_use_open_hand_technique.py`; total 275 → 278.
**Description (cont):** Why prone PC's "Hex must survive" assertion is the load-bearing one. The v2.49.51 incapacitation hook fires when a buff with a key in `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS = {paralyzed, incapacitated, stunned, petrified, unconscious, asleep}` lands on a target — it then drops the target's own concentration anchors. Three prior end-to-end tests pinned the POSITIVE case (`paralyzed` via Hold Person, `stunned` via Stunning Strike, `unconscious` via Sleep — Hex dropped in all three). Until this commit, the NEGATIVE case (an installed condition buff whose key ISN'T in the set should NOT drop concentration) was unpinned. Prone is the perfect candidate: it's a condition buff (effects=list, mechanical-state rider), it lands via the same `_install_buff` pipeline, AND it's not in the incapacitating set. If a future refactor accidentally widens the hook to fire on every condition install, this test catches it.
**Description (cont 2):** Why push PC's response shape assertion is the load-bearing one. Push has no `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` entry; the endpoint stashes `spell_slug: "open-hand-push"` in `_save_request_context` and the /respond handler's lookup returns `None`, so no buff installs. This is INTENTIONAL — push grants the monk permission to physically drag the target 15 ft, not to install a status condition. The test asserts `auto_buff_installed == ""` in both the cast response AND the /respond response, AND that Magnus's buff list carries no spurious prone / reaction-denied entries afterwards. Regression guard against a hypothetical future bug where push mode accidentally installs the prone buff (the two modes are similar — easy mistake).
**Description (cont 3):** Why no_reactions PC validates both hub AND sheet mirror. The endpoint's PC branch calls `_install_buff` followed by `_mirror_buffs_to_sheet`. A subtle bug class: install lands in hub but mirror is skipped, leaving the character sheet stale until the next other-buff-install triggers a mirror. The "buffs" endpoint at `GET /character/{id}/buffs` returns both `buffs` (live hub) AND `sheet_buffs` (mirror); asserting on both pins the mirror invariant. Mirrors the same assertion shape used in the v2.49.61 wake-on-damage PC test.
**Description (cont 4):** Verification. Pre-fix: all 3 PC tests didn't exist. Post-test-add: all 3 pass on first run for the deterministic cases; the prone case landed a save failure within 1–3 iterations (DC = 8+3+2 = 13 vs Magnus's DEX +2 → save fails ~55% of attempts). Full regression: 278 harness tests pass (was 275, +3 new). Existing 5 Open Hand NPC + error tests unchanged.

### Added
- `tests/harness/test_use_open_hand_technique.py::test_open_hand_prone_pc_installs_prone` — Prone PC + regression guard that the v2.49.51 hook does NOT fire on a non-incapacitating buff (Hex survives).
- `tests/harness/test_use_open_hand_technique.py::test_open_hand_push_pc_no_buff` — push PC + no-install assertion (push has no `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` entry).
- `tests/harness/test_use_open_hand_technique.py::test_open_hand_no_reactions_pc` — no_reactions PC + hub-AND-sheet-mirror install + 🫷 public log assertion.
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — three new rows under `test_use_open_hand_technique.py`; total 275 → 278.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Test-only addition. Production code untouched.
- **Negative branch of the v2.49.51 hook now pinned.** Four sites total: paralyzed install (positive), stunned install (positive, concentration=False), unconscious install (positive, no-save / Sleep), prone install (negative — must NOT fire). The hook's `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS` membership check is now end-to-end tested in both directions.

### Filed
- **All v2.49.57 Open Hand filed items now closed.** Remaining sub-items (Wholeness of Body / Tranquility / Quivering Palm subclass features at Lv 6 / 11 / 17) carried forward.
- **`push_authorized` cast-card UI** — still open; coupled to ruler/range Phase 2 (drag-target-15-ft prompt benefits from range visualization).

## [2.49.64] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Undead + charm-immune creatures are immune to Sleep, per RAW.** Closes the v2.49.58 filed item — the last open one in the Sleep block. RAW PHB Sleep: "Undead and creatures immune to being charmed aren't affected by this spell." New `_is_sleep_immune` helper inspects the target's stat block: for NPCs via the monster template (resolves the SRD JSON overlay through `local_content` to read `race` + `condition_immunities`), for PCs via the character sheet. Immune targets are added to the `unaffected` response array with `reason: "undead"` or `reason: "charm_immune"` (undead trumps charm-immune in reporting because most undead are also charm-immune; "undead" is the more specific cause). Same commit adds Skeleton (Undead) + Doppelganger (Monstrosity + charm-immune) templates to the demo seed + a SQL backfill so the running campaign carries them. 3 new harness tests pin both immunity branches + a regression guard that plain humanoids still get Sleep'd. PATCH — additive helper + additive demo data; existing routes and broadcast shapes unchanged.
**Description:** Five edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_is_sleep_immune` (NEW helper, ~40 lines). NPCs route through `_monster_template_to_sheet` to get the SRD-overlaid stat block; checks `race` for the substring "undead" + `condition_immunities` for any entry containing "charm" (case-insensitive). PCs route through the character sheet using the same `_check_sheet` inner function. Returns `(is_immune, reason)` with reason as `"undead"` / `"charm_immune"` / `""`. **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::cast_sleep` — target-resolution loop now calls `_is_sleep_immune` after the already-unconscious skip and BEFORE the HP-pool walk. Immune targets land in a new `immune_unaffected` list; the existing `unaffected` array starts with that list so the final response carries both immunity-driven and HP-driven misses in one place. **(3)** `app/demo_seed.py::seed_token_templates` — added Skeleton + Doppelganger to the specs list. Both resolve via shipped SRD JSONs (`skeleton.json`: type=Undead; `doppelganger.json`: type=Monstrosity, condition_immunities="charmed"). **(4)** SQL backfill: idempotent INSERT into `token_templates` for Skeleton (id=5) + Doppelganger (id=6) in the running demo so harness tests can target them without a full demo reseed (still blocked by the FK bug filed in v2.49.63). **(5)** `tests/harness/test_cast_sleep_immunity.py` (NEW, 3 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why `race` substring rather than a structured `creature_type` field. `_monster_dict_to_sheet` at line 16082 sets `sheet["race"] = f"{size} {type}"` — concatenated form like "Medium Undead" or "Medium Humanoid". There's no separate `sheet["type"]` field today. Substring "undead" check on the lowercased race is robust to capitalization variants ("Medium Undead", "Medium undead") and to size variants (Tiny / Small / Medium / Large / Huge / Gargantuan undead all match). Could add a structured field in a refactor pass, but for this filter the substring check is correct and minimal. Same approach applies to "charm" substring on condition immunities to catch "charmed" + future hypothetical wordings.
**Description (cont 2):** Why the helper checks BOTH the monster template AND the character sheet (NPC vs. PC). RAW Sleep affects "any creature" — including PC allies caught in the radius. PCs RAW today don't have charm immunity (no PC race in the SRD does), but the helper covers them defensively in case a future feat / homebrew race adds it. The PC branch reads `char.sheet["race"]` + `char.sheet["condition_immunities"]` — the latter is an empty list for every demo PC, so the branch is a no-op in practice for stock seeds. Future-proof + cheap.
**Description (cont 3):** Why immune targets go in `unaffected` with a reason rather than being silently filtered. The cast card needs to render "X was immune to Sleep (undead)" so the caster knows why their AoE didn't hit X. Silently filtering would make the spell feel buggy ("I clicked X but nothing happened"). Following the existing `unaffected[i].reason = "hp_above_pool_remaining"` precedent — every miss has a named reason. The "already-unconscious" case is the one exception, where the target is genuinely removed from consideration per RAW ("ignoring unconscious creatures"); immune creatures aren't ignored — they're considered and rejected. The two semantics are RAW-distinct and the response shape matches.
**Description (cont 4):** Why Skeleton + Doppelganger as the demo additions. The exclusion needs two branches tested independently: undead AND non-undead-but-charm-immune. Skeleton: type=Undead, condition_immunities=`exhaustion, poisoned` — exercises the undead-branch cleanly (the charm-immune check on Skeleton would return False because it's not charm-immune; the undead check fires first by helper ordering). Doppelganger: type=Monstrosity, condition_immunities=`charmed` — exercises the charm-immune branch with a non-undead creature, so we know the two branches are independent. Picked Doppelganger over Ghoul (which is undead AND charm-immune) for clarity: Ghoul would trip the undead branch first, masking whether the charm-immune branch even works.
**Description (cont 5):** Why "undead" reason wins over "charm_immune" when both apply. Helper checks undead first (race substring), then condition_immunities. Most undead RAW are also charm-immune (ghouls, wraiths, etc.). Returning "undead" as the reason gives the GM the more specific / lore-relevant cause; "charm_immune" would correctly describe a doppelganger or solar but is the wrong word for a skeleton. Tie-breaking by order matches "most specific cause first" — same convention as `_apply_hp_change`'s death-save state precedence.
**Description (cont 6):** Why the SQL backfill rather than a full demo reseed. The demo reseed has the FK-ordering bug filed in v2.49.63. Forcing a fresh reseed risks data loss for any in-flight work in the demo (other characters' HP, AoE markers, etc.). The INSERT is idempotent (`NOT EXISTS` guard on the name) and surgical — only the two new template rows are touched. Future demo reseeds (once the FK bug is fixed) will pick up the seed-file additions on next boot.
**Description (cont 7):** Verification. Pre-fix: each new test failed because either (a) the templates didn't exist in the running demo, or (b) `cast_sleep` had no immunity check so Skeleton/Doppelganger landed in `affected`. After the helper + seed + SQL backfill: all 3 pass. Full regression: 275 harness tests pass (was 272, +3 new). No regressions on existing Sleep / damage / buff tests.

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_is_sleep_immune` — helper checking monster template (NPC) or character sheet (PC) for `race contains "undead"` or `condition_immunities contains "charm"`. Returns `(is_immune, reason)`.
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::cast_sleep` — target-resolution loop now adds immune targets to `unaffected` with `reason="undead"` / `"charm_immune"`.
- `app/demo_seed.py::seed_token_templates` — Skeleton + Doppelganger added.
- `tests/harness/test_cast_sleep_immunity.py` — 3 tests (undead excluded / charm-immune excluded / regular humanoid affected).
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 272 → 275.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Additive helper + additive seed entries + additive `unaffected[i].reason` values (`undead` / `charm_immune` join the existing `hp_above_pool_remaining`). No existing route or broadcast shape changed.
- **All v2.49.58 Sleep-block filed items now closed.** Wake-on-damage (v2.49.61), wake-via-shake (v2.49.62), Sleep on BSW spell lists (v2.49.63), undead/charm-immune (this commit). Only the cross-cutting "20-ft radius enforcement" item remains, gated on the ruler/range plan's Phase 2 implementation.
- **Helper is reusable.** Future spells with similar exclusions (Calm Emotions targets only humanoids + beasts; Charm Person targets only humanoids; etc.) can grow the same helper pattern — extract `_check_sheet` further if a third caller emerges.

### Filed
- **Structured `creature_type` field on the projected NPC sheet** — today the type lives in `race` as a concatenated "Medium Undead" string. A separate `sheet["creature_type"]` field would simplify this filter and others. Filed for a refactor pass.
- **Calm Emotions / Charm Person / Geas exclusion lists** — similar shape; same helper pattern. Filed for when those spells get endpoints.
- **20-ft radius enforcement for Sleep** — still open. Gated on the ruler/range plan's Phase 2.

## [2.49.62] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Add `/shake_awake` — third RAW Sleep wake branch.** Closes the v2.49.61 filed "wake-via-shake" item. RAW Sleep: "each creature affected by this spell falls unconscious until the spell ends, the sleeper takes damage, OR SOMEONE USES AN ACTION TO SHAKE OR SLAP THE SLEEPER AWAKE." Branch 2 (damage) shipped in v2.49.61; this commit lands branch 3. New endpoint `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/shake_awake` — any class can invoke (RAW "someone"), costs 1 action, requires the target to have a Sleep-sourced Unconscious buff. Validates Phase 4 action gate; 409 `not_asleep` when the target has no matching buff. On success: removes the buff (PC: `_remove_buff` + sheet mirror; NPC: hub mutation + `battle_update`), marks the action slot, emits a public 🤚 roll-log entry. 4 new harness tests pin NPC + PC wake + two 409 paths. PATCH — additive endpoint; no API contract change.
**Description:** Two edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::shake_awake` — new endpoint placed right after `cast_sleep`. Body `{character_id, target_combatant_id?, target_character_id?, target_name?, override?}`. Resolves target via `_lookup_combatant` (falls back to hub-state PC search by `char_id` when only `target_character_id` is given). Filters `target.buffs` for `key in ("unconscious", "asleep") AND source_spell == "Sleep"`; returns 409 `not_asleep` with `target_name` + `reason` field when nothing matches. Phase 4 action gate mirrors `cast_hex` exactly (overrideable unless strict mode). Buff removal mirrors `_wake_sleeping_on_damage`'s PC + NPC branches; logs are identical to the damage-wake hook but with a 🤚 emoji + "shakes ... awake" phrasing. **(2)** `tests/harness/test_shake_awake.py` (NEW, 4 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why the buff filter uses the same `source_spell == "Sleep"` gate as the damage hook. Same RAW reason: shaking a dying-at-0-HP creature doesn't wake them (their Unconscious is the dying state, not a Sleep effect). Future endpoints that install Unconscious via other mechanisms (Power Word Knockout, Druid Sleep Touch, etc.) might or might not respond to shake — RAW decides per spell. Same conservative default as the damage hook: only fire for the exact Sleep source. The two hooks now share five-way symmetric semantics: install (cast_sleep) + damage-wake (_wake_sleeping_on_damage) + shake-wake (this endpoint) all key on the same `source_spell` tag.
**Description (cont 2):** Why no class restriction. RAW says "someone uses an action" — not "another caster," not "a friendly creature," literally any creature. The fighter can shake the sorcerer awake; the rogue can shake an enemy bandit awake to interrogate them; the sleeping bandit's ally bandit can shake them awake on its turn. Class-gating would be a RAW violation. The action cost is the only gate on misuse — a PC can shake their own ally awake but they spend their action doing it instead of attacking.
**Description (cont 3):** Why no range check. The ruler/range plan (v2.49.59, `docs/plans/ruler-and-range.md`) Phase 2 will add range enforcement on cast/attack endpoints; the shake-awake endpoint should be wired in at that time (5 ft melee reach, RAW). For now the endpoint trusts the caller — same convention as Stunning Strike + Open Hand Technique's "must follow a hit" gate. Filed as a Phase 2 dependency.
**Description (cont 4):** Why 🤚 emoji + public log visibility. Matches the 🌅 damage-wake convention from v2.49.61: table-visible event (a sleeper visibly snaps awake; the table sees a roll). 🤚 connotes the physical shake action; 🌅 connotes the dawn-of-consciousness moment. Distinct emoji so a GM scanning the roll log can tell at a glance how the sleeper woke (damaged vs. shaken). Same visibility (PUBLIC); same envelope (`type: "roll"`); same broadcast pattern.
**Description (cont 5):** Test design. Pre-seeds the Sleep buff via `/battle` PUT (same approach as test_sleep_wake_on_damage.py — deterministic, no retry loop on the install). Action gate is overrideable by default since the test scenarios don't care about chip state; one test could be added later to pin the 409 over_budget path but it's structurally identical to the cast_hex / cast_sleep gate already pinned elsewhere. The "non_sleep_unconscious" 409 test is the load-bearing regression guard — if a future bug widens the buff filter, this catches it before it ships.
**Description (cont 6):** Verification. Ran pre-fix: all 4 tests failed with 404 (endpoint missing). Post-fix: all 4 pass. Full regression: 269 harness tests pass (was 265, +4 new). No regressions on damage / buff / sleep / concentration tests.

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::shake_awake` — new endpoint `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/shake_awake`. Any class; costs 1 action; requires Sleep-sourced Unconscious buff on the target.
- `tests/harness/test_shake_awake.py` — 4 tests (NPC wake / PC wake / not_asleep no buff / not_asleep generic unconscious).
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 265 → 269.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive endpoint. New 🤚 roll-log entry but rides on the existing `type: "roll"` envelope; clients already render those.
- **All three RAW Sleep wake branches now pinned.** (1) Spell duration runs out (timer in buff; client tick decrements) — covered by existing duration handling. (2) Sleeper takes damage — v2.49.61. (3) Action to shake awake — this commit.
- **No range enforcement.** Filed as a Phase 2 ruler/range dependency.

### Filed
- **Range check on `/shake_awake`** — 5 ft melee reach (RAW). Adds to Phase 2 of the ruler/range plan.
- **Self-shake** — RAW unclear: can a sleeper shake themself awake? Probably not (they're unconscious and can't take actions). The endpoint today doesn't gate on shaker != target; a self-shake would succeed because the target's buff exists and the shaker's action gate is independent. Marginal; file for later if it surfaces.
- **Undead / charm-immune exclusion for Sleep targeting** — still open from v2.49.58.
- **Sleep on Bard / Sorcerer / Warlock spell lists** — still open from v2.49.58.

## [2.49.61] - 2026-05-22

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Wake sleeping creatures on damage — RAW Sleep ends the slumber when the sleeper takes damage.** Closes the v2.49.58 "wake-on-damage" filed item. New helper `_wake_sleeping_on_damage` called from both branches of `_apply_damage_to_combatant`. Scoped tightly: only removes Unconscious buffs with `source_spell == "Sleep"` — other Unconscious sources (future Power Word Knockout, future druid Sleep Touch, etc.) are left alone. Zero-damage hits (resistance reduced to 0) don't wake. Emits a public 🌅 roll-log entry so the GM + table see the cause. Same commit fixes a pre-existing latent bug in `_resistance_halve`: condition buffs (Paralyzed, Stunned, Sleep-Unconscious) carry `effects` as a string list, but the function assumed dict; it now skips non-dict effects. Bug had been latent since the first condition buff shipped because no prior test damaged a creature carrying a condition buff. 3 new harness tests + the latent-bug fix. PATCH — additive hook + bug fix; no API contract change.
**Description:** Three edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_wake_sleeping_on_damage` (NEW helper, ~80 lines). Body: looks up the target combatant in hub state by `character_id` (PC) or `combatant_id` (NPC), filters buffs to those with key in (`unconscious`, `asleep`) AND `source_spell == "Sleep"`, removes them. PC path routes through `_remove_buff` (buff_update broadcast + paired-cleanup, no-op for concentration=False); NPC path mutates the buff list directly + broadcasts `battle_update` with `force_gm_sync=True` (mirrors v2.49.40 NPC HP-damage pattern). PC also calls `_mirror_buffs_to_sheet` so the sheet doesn't carry stale `_buffs_active` entries. Public 🌅 roll-log entry fires after the removal. Short-circuits on `damage_applied <= 0` and on missing target. **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_apply_damage_to_combatant` — added `await _wake_sleeping_on_damage(...)` call in both branches, after the damage broadcast. **(3)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_resistance_halve` — guard `effects` with `isinstance(effects, dict)` before calling `.get("resistance_to")`. **(4)** `tests/harness/test_sleep_wake_on_damage.py` (NEW, 3 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why the helper at the damage-pipeline level, not at the buff-install level. The wake check is a *consequence* of damage, not a property of the buff. Putting the logic inside `_install_buff` or `_remove_buff` would put a "check for damage application" check inside a buff-state primitive — wrong direction of dependency. The damage pipeline is the right call site: every damage source (weapon attack, spell damage, AoE save-for-half, GM manual HP edit through future endpoints) routes through `_apply_damage_to_combatant`, so wiring the hook there covers every wake path with one call site per branch.
**Description (cont 2):** Why scope to `source_spell == "Sleep"` rather than wake on every Unconscious. Sleep's RAW "damage wakes" rule is spell-specific — it's listed in Sleep's text, not in the Unconscious condition's text. A future "Power Word Knockout" or "Druid Sleep Touch" or a homebrew "permanent magical slumber" might install Unconscious with different wake-on-damage semantics (or none — Power Word Knockout RAW is permanent until ended by another spell). The conservative default is to only fire the wake on the exact RAW source. Future endpoints add their own source_spell tags and the helper can be extended.
**Description (cont 3):** Why the `_resistance_halve` latent-bug fix lands in the same commit. The new wake tests are the first to apply damage to a PC carrying a condition buff (Sleep-Unconscious, with `effects: list`). When the damage handler called `_resistance_halve(damage, type, sheet)`, the function iterated `sheet["_buffs_active"]` and tried `effects.get("resistance_to")` — but `effects` was a list. AttributeError → 500. The fix (skip non-dict effects) is two lines; it's a precondition for the wake test to pass. Could ship as a separate commit, but the bug is tightly coupled to the test's damage path — splitting would land "test fails on latent bug" + "fix the latent bug, test now passes" in two commits when one tells the story cleanly.
**Description (cont 4):** Why the latent bug never tripped before. Resistance only applies when the target's sheet has `_buffs_active` entries — the only paths that populate that field are buffs installed via `_install_buff` + `_mirror_buffs_to_sheet`. Condition buffs (Paralyzed, Stunned, Unconscious-from-Sleep) DO go through that path. But the buff installs in test scenarios were never followed by a damage application: test_incapacitation_drops_concentration ends after the Paralyzed install (no damage), test_use_stunning_strike ends after Stunned (no damage), test_cast_sleep ends after Unconscious (no damage). The wake-on-damage test is the FIRST to combine "install a condition buff" + "deal damage to the wearer" in the same test. The bug was waiting for this exact pattern.
**Description (cont 5):** Why the 🌅 wake log is `Visibility.PUBLIC`, not GM-only. Concentration logs (💀, ✋, 🔁) are GM-only because concentration is a private mechanical detail the wizard tracks. Sleep wake-on-damage is a TABLE-VISIBLE event — the bandit was sleeping, you attacked, the table sees a roll, the bandit visibly snaps awake. Hiding that from the players makes the round confusing ("wait, is the bandit asleep or not?"). Public log keeps the table in sync with the canvas.
**Description (cont 6):** Test design. All three tests pre-seed the buff via `/battle` PUT rather than going through `/cast_sleep` end-to-end. Two reasons: (a) deterministic — the wake test doesn't care which combinations of HP / pool roll land the Sleep; the install path is already pinned by `test_cast_sleep.py`. (b) faster — no retry loop on the install. The attack retry loop is still required because hit-roll is random vs target AC; 20 iterations is the same pattern used by the v2.49.55 Stunning Strike happy-path NPC test. Reads the latest state via `gm_ws.buffered("battle_update")[-1]` (the wake fires AFTER the damage broadcast — both arrive in the buffer, the wake one is last). Initially the test used `wait_for("battle_update")` which always returns `hits[0]` (first match in buffer, not next); the bug was caught and fixed by switching to `buffered()[-1]`.
**Description (cont 7):** Verification. Pre-fix: NPC wake test failed with "buff still on bandit"; PC wake test failed with 500 (`_resistance_halve` AttributeError on `effects.get`). Post-fix (both `_wake_sleeping_on_damage` + `_resistance_halve` guard): all 3 wake tests pass. Full regression: 265 harness tests pass (was 262, +3 new); no regressions on existing damage / buff / concentration tests.

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_wake_sleeping_on_damage` — new helper called from both branches of `_apply_damage_to_combatant`. Removes Sleep-sourced Unconscious buffs + emits a public 🌅 wake log.
- `tests/harness/test_sleep_wake_on_damage.py` — 3 tests (NPC wake / PC wake / non-Sleep unconscious preserved).
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 262 → 265.

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_resistance_halve` — guards `effects` against being a list before calling `.get("resistance_to")`. Pre-existing latent bug exposed by the new wake test (first to apply damage to a wearer of a condition buff). All condition buffs (Paralyzed, Stunned, Unconscious-from-Sleep, Charmed, Frightened) carry `effects` as a string list; mechanical buffs (Rage, Hex, Hunter's Mark) carry it as a dict. The check now correctly applies only to dict-shaped effects.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive hook + pure defensive guard. No API contract change; no broadcast shape change beyond the new (additive) 🌅 roll-log entry.
- **Fifth use of the buff-source filter.** Three previous sites filter buffs by `source_char_id` (v2.49.51 / v2.49.53 / v2.49.54). This commit filters by `source_spell` — same semantic shape ("this buff is mine to act on") but keyed on the SPELL name rather than the CASTER. Both filter dimensions matter going forward; codifying them under a single helper would dedupe across all five sites.
- **Public 🌅 visibility, not GM-only.** Wake-on-damage is table-visible (the table sees a damage roll + a sleeper waking); concentration events (💀, ✋, 🔁) are GM-only because concentration is a private detail.

### Filed
- **`source_spell` filter helper** — five sites now filter buffs by some combination of `source_char_id` / `source_spell`. A `_is_own_buff_for(buff, character_id=None, spell_name=None)` helper would dedupe. Punt unless a sixth site lands.
- **Wake-via-shake action** — RAW Sleep also wakes a sleeper when another creature uses an action to shake them. Needs a new `/shake_awake` endpoint (action consumption + remove Sleep-Unconscious from target). Filed for follow-up; for now GM clears via `/end_buff unconscious`.
- **Resistance for condition buffs** — would condition buffs ever advertise damage resistance? Hideous Laughter's prone-and-incapacitated doesn't. Stoneskin (separate spell) installs resistance via a mechanical-effect buff with `effects: dict`. The two shapes are RAW-distinct, so no future condition needs to advertise resistance. The dict-check guard is correct.
- **Undead / immune-to-charm exclusion for Sleep targeting** — still open from v2.49.58.

## [2.49.60] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Add a "restart the app container after every version bump" rule to CLAUDE.md.** Doc-only. The docker dev image bakes the code at build time (no live-reload mount on the `app` service in `docker-compose.yml`), which means a committed version bump doesn't propagate to the running container until `docker compose up -d --build app` runs. Surfaced during this session when the v2.49.55 Stunning Strike endpoint worked but `/version` reported v2.49.54 — the container had been built between commits, leaving the visible version stale. Documenting the rebuild as an explicit step in the per-commit workflow makes it impossible to forget AND surfaces the rationale (harness tests at `http://localhost:8013` talk to the container, not in-process code; a stale container masks new-endpoint regressions and inline-migration runs). Rule lives next to the existing "Always create the git commit at the end of the change" rule because both describe the per-commit deploy cadence. PATCH — docs-only.
**Description:** One edit. **(1)** `CLAUDE.md` — new paragraph "Restart the app container after every version bump" appended to the "Always update the changelog and version when making changes" section. Names the rebuild command (`docker compose up -d --build app`), the verification command (`curl -s http://localhost:8013/version`), and the expected timing (5–15 s on Apple Silicon). Calls out three failure modes the rebuild prevents: (a) harness tests against stale code returning 404 for new endpoints, (b) manual click-through verification on stale code, (c) `SCHEMA_VERSION` bumps that leave the DB un-migrated because `_apply_inline_migrations` only fires on container boot. Warns against `docker compose down -v` as a destructive workaround (would wipe the postgres volume + the demo seed has known FK-ordering bugs on partial-state replays).
**Description (cont):** Why CLAUDE.md rather than a settings.json hook. The user explicitly requested adding the rule to "your claude file" — they want this as a behavioral guideline I read at the start of every session, not a harness-executed automation. A pre/post-commit hook would be more reliable (no chance of me forgetting) but adds complexity: the hook would have to detect a version bump (parse `version.py`), then run a 30-second docker rebuild as part of the commit cycle, blocking the next prompt. CLAUDE.md keeps the rule visible without coupling the rebuild to the commit lifecycle — I run it explicitly after each commit instead.
**Description (cont 2):** Why the rule applies to doc-only commits too. The temptation is to skip the rebuild when "no code changed" — but `version.py` IS code (`APP_VERSION` is imported by `/version`, `/healthz`, and the runtime banner). A doc-only commit that bumps `APP_VERSION` leaves the running container reporting the OLD version, which is wrong for any observer (browser client polling for updates, harness asserting on `/version`, GM looking at the banner). The rule is universal — "every version bump = rebuild" — to avoid carving out exceptions that drift.
**Description (cont 3):** Verification. Pre-fix: CLAUDE.md had no rebuild guidance; the docker container could (and did) lag the source repo by several commits without warning. Post-fix: the rule lives in CLAUDE.md and is the second-to-last paragraph in the version-management section — the natural reading order is "bump → CHANGELOG → README → commit → restart." Doc-only; no functional change. Container restart performed as part of this commit per the new rule.

### Added
- `CLAUDE.md` — new "Restart the app container after every version bump" paragraph in the version-management section. Names the rebuild command + verification command + three failure modes the rule prevents.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Doc-only. No code changes.
- **Self-applying.** This commit itself bumps the version, so the rule kicks in immediately — the container is rebuilt as part of landing this commit.

ASCII mockups are crude but unambiguous (no rendering dependency), and the file-path index at the end gives the implementation agent exact pixel coordinates (e.g. "insert above the drawer tab bar at `tabletop.html:1216`"). - Token edge vs. token center (recommend: center, add edge mode in Phase 3 if asked).
- Cover / line-of-sight (out of scope — separate massive feature).
- Should range-check fire before or after slot consumption (recommend: before; matches existing 409 gate ordering).
- Should the demo seed include a range-demo encounter (recommend: yes, in Phase 2's implementation commit).
**Description (cont 6):** What's NOT covered (filed for follow-up plans):

- Movement-range enforcement (today `token_move` reports distance via WS but doesn't BLOCK; could add per-turn movement budget enforcement).

## [2.49.58] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Add the Sleep spell — custom HP-pool targeting.** Closes the "Sleep — still absent" filed item from v2.49.55–v2.49.57. RAW (PHB Sleep, 1st-level enchantment, bard/sorcerer/warlock/wizard): roll 5d8 (+2d8 per slot level above 1st) as an HP pool; sort candidate creatures by ascending current HP, ignoring already-unconscious ones; walk the list and put each affected creature to sleep, subtracting their HP from the pool, until the pool is exhausted or there are no candidates left. No save, no concentration. New endpoint `POST /cast_sleep` (dedicated, NOT routed through `/cast_spell` because the HP-pool selector doesn't fit either save-or-suck or save-for-half). The Unconscious key is already in `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS`, so a PC sleeper drops their own concentration via the v2.49.51 hook + emits 💀 — the test pins this end-to-end for the first time on the no-save install path. Also adds Sleep to Thalindra's demo spell list (appended, so existing FIREBALL_INDEX = 7 / Counterspell index assumptions in other harness tests stay intact). 8 new harness tests pin the pool math + ordering invariant + drop-concentration hook + 409 paths. PATCH — additive endpoint + additive seed-list entry; no existing routes or shapes change.
**Description:** Three edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::cast_sleep` (NEW). Body: `{character_id, class_slug, slot_level, target_combatant_ids, override?}`. Validates class (wizard/bard/sorcerer/warlock) + Sleep on the spell list + slot at requested level + Phase 4 action gate (overrideable). Rolls 5d8 + 2d8/level, resolves targets via `_lookup_combatant`, skips already-unconscious + zero-HP, sorts ascending, walks the list installing `unconscious` buffs via `_install_buff` (PC) or `_install_buff_on_combatant_id` (NPC). Marks the action slot + broadcasts a public `roll` event naming the pool + affected list + a `spell_slot_update`. **(2)** `app/demo_seed.py::_wizard_sheet` — appended Sleep to Thalindra's spells. Existing `FIREBALL_INDEX = 7` and Counterspell index references in harness tests are preserved because Sleep lands at index 10 (or 9 in any DB missing Lightning Bolt). **(3)** `tests/harness/test_cast_sleep.py` (NEW, 8 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why a dedicated endpoint rather than routing through `/cast_spell`. Sleep is the only PHB 5e spell with HP-pool targeting; there's no second spell that would amortize a generalized pipeline. `/cast_spell` already branches on save-or-suck vs. save-for-half vs. attack-roll vs. AoE; adding a fifth "HP-pool" branch would tangle the cast-spell handler further. Dedicated endpoint (~280 LOC vs. ~50 LOC of branching in cast_spell, but isolated) follows the cast_hex pattern: Hex also doesn't fit cast_spell's generic shape (unique concentration-buff effects + ability picker).
**Description (cont 2):** Why dice-independent assertions in the ordering test. The pool roll is 5d8 — min 5, max 40, avg 22.5. Asserting a specific affected count would flake. Instead the ordering test asserts the invariants that hold for ANY pool ≥ 5: (a) non-decreasing HP order in `affected`, (b) `sum(affected.hp) <= pool_total`, (c) first `unaffected` (if any) has `hp > pool_remaining` at stop time. Pool=5 → 1+2 affected (3 unaffected); pool=20 → all 3 affected. Both satisfy all three invariants. The "happy path NPC" test uses HP=5 + 5d8 (min=5) for a single-target always-affected case — guaranteed without invariant trickery.
**Description (cont 3):** Why already-unconscious targets are skipped entirely (not "added to unaffected"). RAW: "Creatures within 20 feet of a point you choose within range are affected in ascending order of their current hit points (**ignoring unconscious creatures**)." Skipped from the ordering AND the response — the spell doesn't waste pool on already-asleep creatures, and the response shouldn't report them as "not affected" (which would imply they were considered). The test asserts the already-unconscious bandit appears in neither `affected` nor `unaffected` — clear semantics for the cast-card UI.
**Description (cont 4):** Why this pins the v2.49.51 hook for the third time, and what's new about this branch. v2.49.51 covers the hook generically. The two prior end-to-end tests pin it for: (a) Hold Person (concentration=True, save-or-suck via /cast_spell PC roll_request), (b) Stunning Strike (concentration=False, save-or-suck via /use_stunning_strike PC roll_request). Sleep is the **first no-save** path: the install isn't gated on a saving throw; Thalindra picks the targets and they sleep based on pool math. The hook fires the same way (key="unconscious" matches `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS`), but exercised through the no-save call site rather than the save-or-suck pipeline. Reaffirms that the hook is install-site-agnostic.
**Description (cont 5):** Why Thalindra's seed list adds Sleep at the END. Existing harness tests reference `FIREBALL_INDEX = 7` and other hardcoded spell positions. Inserting Sleep at index 3 (next to Magic Missile, alphabetical-by-level) would shift Fireball to index 8 and break every cast-spell-aoe test. Appending keeps every existing index stable.
**Description (cont 6):** What's NOT modelled here. **Undead / immune-to-charm exclusion** — RAW excludes undead + creatures immune to charm. SimpleVTT doesn't track creature-type immunities consistently, so v1 trusts the GM to deselect inappropriate targets via the candidate-list input. **Wake-on-damage** — RAW: "the sleeper takes damage [...] [wakes them] awake." The existing damage pipeline doesn't auto-clear the Unconscious buff on damage; the GM runs `/end_buff unconscious` manually. **Wake-via-shake** — no `/shake_awake` endpoint; `/end_buff unconscious` covers it for now. **20-ft radius enforcement** — no spatial range yet; the candidate list IS the radius from the GM's perspective (filed as coupled to the ruler/range work being planned separately).
**Description (cont 7):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: all 8 failed with 404 (endpoint missing) + 409 spell_not_known (Sleep not on Thalindra's list). Post-fix: all 8 pass. Full regression: 262 harness tests pass total (was 254, +8 new) — one pre-existing flaky attack-crit test occasionally trips; not my doing and not load-bearing. 33 encounter-sim tests unchanged.

### Added
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::cast_sleep` — new endpoint `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/cast_sleep`. Validates class + Sleep on list + slot + Phase 4 gate; rolls 5d8 + 2d8/level pool; sorts targets by ascending current HP, skips already-unconscious; walks the list installing Unconscious via `_install_buff` (PC) / `_install_buff_on_combatant_id` (NPC).
- `app/demo_seed.py::_wizard_sheet` — Sleep appended to Thalindra's spell list (`_slug: "sleep"`, level 1, prepared, 1 action). Appended to preserve existing harness spell-index references.
- `tests/harness/test_cast_sleep.py` — 8 tests (happy path NPC / ordering invariant / high HP skip / already-unconscious skip / drops PC concentration / upcast scales pool / no_slot / wrong_class).
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 254 → 262.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure additive: new endpoint, new seed-list entry appended at the end. Existing `/cast_spell` behavior + every other endpoint unchanged. Existing harness `FIREBALL_INDEX = 7` / Counterspell index assumptions preserved by appending Sleep.
- **Third install-site for the v2.49.51 hook.** First was Hold Person (concentration=True save-or-suck PC), second was Stunning Strike (concentration=False save-or-suck PC), third is Sleep (no-save, no concentration, install-by-pool-math). Same hook fires; same 💀 log emits; install-site-agnostic.
- **Dice path uses the seeded RNG.** `dice_mod.roll("5d8")` honors the `DICE_SEED` env var so seeded test runs would be deterministic. The harness tests assert dice-independent invariants anyway — no DICE_SEED needed.

### Filed
- **Undead / immune-to-charm exclusion** — needs creature-type tagging on monster templates to enforce automatically. v1 trusts the GM to deselect inappropriate targets.
- **Wake-on-damage** — when a sleeper takes damage, RAW wakes them. The damage pipeline could check for `unconscious` source=`Sleep` and call `_remove_buff` after applying damage. Out of scope here.
- **Wake-via-shake** — `/shake_awake` endpoint that takes another creature's action to wake a sleeping ally. Or just `/end_buff unconscious` for now.

## [2.49.57] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Add Monk Open Hand Technique (Way of the Open Hand, Lv 3+ subclass feature).** Closes the "Open Hand Technique" filed item from v2.49.55. RAW: when monk hits with a Flurry of Blows attack, they may impose one of three riders — Prone (DEX save), Push 15 ft (STR save), or No Reactions (no save, 1 turn). No additional ki cost (the Flurry already paid). New endpoint `POST /use_open_hand_technique` takes a `mode` param (`prone` | `push` | `no_reactions`). Prone routes through the save-or-suck pipeline using a new `open-hand-prone` entry in `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP`. Push uses the same pipeline structurally but has NO map entry — the response carries `push_authorized` so the GM UI can drag the token; no buff installs. No Reactions skips the save entirely and installs a `reaction-denied` buff inline (`concentration: False`, `duration_rounds: 1`) plus a public roll-log entry. 5 new harness tests pin all three modes + 409 wrong_class + 400 bad_mode. PATCH — additive endpoint; existing routes and broadcast shapes unchanged.
**Description:** Three edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` — added `"open-hand-prone"` entry. `key: "prone"`, `concentration: False`, `duration_rounds: 10` (Prone has no RAW timer — ends when the prone creature spends half movement to stand; 10 rounds is a generous default and the GM ends it via `/end_buff`). Effects list summarizes the RAW prone-condition rider. Crucially **not** in `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS` — Prone constrains movement / grants advantage at melee + disadvantage at range, but doesn't incapacitate. **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::use_open_hand_technique` — new `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/use_open_hand_technique` endpoint. Validates monk + Way of the Open Hand + Lv 3+. Branches on `mode`: no_reactions is the early-return inline-install path (mirrors `/use_rage` / `/use_bardic_inspiration` "install + announce"); prone + push share the save pipeline (same DC math + roll_request setup as Stunning Strike). **(3)** `tests/harness/test_use_open_hand_technique.py` (NEW, 5 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why one endpoint with a `mode` param rather than three separate endpoints. RAW the three options are one feature with one "choose at use time" gate. Splitting into `/use_open_hand_prone` / `/use_open_hand_push` / `/use_open_hand_no_reactions` would triple the validation boilerplate (monk + subclass + level + target lookup all repeat) and force three almost-identical chat-card buttons. A single endpoint with a discriminator keeps the validation in one place + matches how the future UI surfaces the feature (one button with a popover that picks the mode). The mode whitelist (`prone` / `push` / `no_reactions`) is the same shape as `class_slug` parameters on existing multi-class spell-cast endpoints.
**Description (cont 2):** Why push has no `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` entry. Push doesn't install a buff — it grants the monk permission to physically move the target up to 15 ft. SimpleVTT today doesn't enforce movement, so the push is a GM-facing "drag the token" instruction. The response carries `push_authorized: True` (on save fail) / `False` (on pass) so the cast-card UI can render a "Drag target up to 15 ft from monk" prompt. For PC targets the save is rolled by the player via roll_request; the GM observes the save total in the roll log and acts (the /respond handler's install branch is a no-op because `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP.get("open-hand-push")` is None). For NPC targets the server rolls inline and `push_authorized` ships in the same response.
**Description (cont 3):** Why no_reactions skips the save pipeline entirely. RAW has no save — the rider just lands. Routing through the save-or-suck pipeline would mean creating a sham DC=0 roll_request with no decision branches; cleaner to install inline + broadcast a public roll-log entry. **Schema version:** 56

Stunned is RAW `concentration: False` (1-turn condition, not a sustained spell) — so this commit also validates the v2.49.51 incapacitation hook's "concentration=False" branch end-to-end: the Stunned install on a PC target via the existing roll_request → /respond pipeline drops the PC's own concentration anchors via the `_install_buff` v2.49.51 path. Endpoint reuses the cast_spell save-or-suck pipeline by routing through `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP["stunning-strike"]` (new entry, slug treated as a class-feature identifier — the lookup is slug-keyed and doesn't care whether the source is a spell or a feature). NPC targets get a server-rolled save inline. PC targets get a roll_request the player owner /responds to (same path as Hold Person). 3 new harness tests pin happy-path NPC + wrong_class + no_ki. PATCH — additive endpoint; existing routes and broadcast shapes unchanged.
**Description:** Three edits. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` — added a new `"stunning-strike"` entry with `key: "stunned"`, `concentration: False`, `duration_rounds: 1`, RAW effects list. The slug is a class-feature identifier; the existing pipeline doesn't care whether it's a spell or a feature, just looks it up by slug. **(2)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::use_stunning_strike` — new `POST /api/campaign/{cid}/use_stunning_strike` endpoint. Body: `{character_id, target_combatant_id?, target_character_id?, target_name?}`. Validates monk class + level >= 5 + ki >= 1, then spends 1 ki, computes save DC = 8 + monk prof + monk WIS mod, and routes through either the NPC server-rolled save path (mirrors cast_spell line ~7440) or the PC roll_request path (mirrors line ~7392). On fail the existing save-or-suck install code at line ~6564 picks up the slug from `_save_request_context` and installs Stunned via `_install_buff` (PC) / `_install_buff_on_combatant_id` (NPC inline above). Stunning Strike is a free interrupt RAW, so no action / bonus / reaction slot is consumed (only ki). **(3)** `tests/harness/test_use_stunning_strike.py` (NEW, 3 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why route through `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP` rather than write a bespoke install. The save-or-suck pipeline already handles three coupled concerns: (a) the DC computation + save-roll broadcast + result correlation back to the cast card, (b) the buff dict construction with correct source/duration/concentration/effects, (c) the v2.49.51 incapacitation hook firing via `_install_buff`. Reusing the pipeline keeps Stunning Strike consistent with Hold Person etc.: a future GM-facing "save events" filter will surface stuns the same way it surfaces hold-persons. Cost: a slug naming convention that conflates "spell" and "class feature." Acceptable trade.
**Description (cont 2):** Why Stunning Strike is the right first non-concentration incapacitating impl. Alternatives considered: **Sleep** — 1d8-per-slot HP pool affects creatures by ascending HP, no save, unique selection mechanic that doesn't fit any existing endpoint pattern; would need a custom targeting flow (~3× the LOC). **Power Word Stun** — 150-HP threshold then 1-CHA-save mechanic, narrower use case, requires high-level seed setup. **Banishment** — RAW debatable on incapacitation; impl in SimpleVTT today is removal-from-init (different code path entirely). Stunning Strike: single-target, CON save, simple ki cost, monk already in demo, fits the existing save-or-suck pipeline, validates the v2.49.51 hook's non-concentration branch. Cleanest unit of work.
**Description (cont 3):** Why no slot consumption. RAW: "When you hit another creature with a melee weapon attack, you can spend 1 ki point to attempt a stunning strike." It's an interrupt that piggybacks on an attack, not an action of its own. The attack itself consumes the action; Stunning Strike is the rider. The endpoint enforces ki consumption but skips action / bonus / reaction marking. (Compare /use_lay_on_hands which marks the action slot — Lay on Hands IS the paladin's action, RAW.) The "must follow a hit" constraint is filed for the client-side UI (the chat-card "Stun?" button should only appear after a successful melee hit); the endpoint itself trusts the caller, matching the override-friendly convention of other class-feature endpoints.
**Description (cont 4):** Test strategy. The test asserts (a) endpoint response shape, (b) buff key + `concentration: False` + `source_char_id` on the broadcast buff, (c) WS `battle_update` envelope. The 409 paths are deterministic (no dice) — single-call assertions.
**Description (cont 5):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: all 3 failed with 404 ("endpoint not found"). Post-fix: all 3 pass. Full regression: 248 harness tests pass (was 245, +3 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass.

## [2.49.54] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **Fix RAW bug: swap loop wrongly dropped paired conditions from other casters.** Closes the bug filed in v2.49.53. PHB p.203 RAW: "you can only concentrate on ONE spell at a time" applies per-caster. A paired condition buff on a victim — e.g. Paralyzed on a Hold Person victim, where `source_char_id` is the enemy caster — is sustained by the SOURCE caster's concentration, not the victim's. The victim casting a new concentration spell of their own should NOT drop the paired condition (otherwise a Held victim could "shake off" being Held by casting Hex, which is wrong RAW + bad gameplay). Pre-fix, `_install_buff`'s swap loop dropped every `concentration: True` buff on the combatant when a new concentration buff landed, regardless of who sourced the existing ones. v2.49.53 already added the source filter to the 🔁 log emission (so the audit was correct); v2.49.54 applies the same filter to the underlying BEHAVIOR so the buff is preserved, not just the log. The fix is a 5-line addition inside the swap loop: when `b.get("source_char_id")` is non-null and != self, append the buff to `new_list` instead of marking it as replaced. 2 new harness tests pin the new behavior + a regression guard for legitimate own-anchor swaps. PATCH — bug fix; no schema or API contract change.
**Description:** Two edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_install_buff` swap loop — inside the `if is_concentration and b.get("concentration"):` branch, added a new check before marking the buff as replaced: if `b.get("source_char_id")` is non-null AND != `character_id`, append the buff to `new_list` (preserve it) and `continue` instead of falling through to the replace path. This filter mirrors the one already applied to (a) `_drop_caster_concentration` (v2.49.51) and (b) the v2.49.53 🔁 log emission — three places now share the same "is this buff actually owned by this combatant?" predicate. **(2)** `tests/harness/test_swap_preserves_paired_buffs.py` (NEW, 2 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why the fix landed via the swap loop rather than upstream. The bug class is: "concentration-flagged buffs on a combatant might be owned by them OR by someone else." Every code path that iterates `target.get("buffs")` and treats `concentration: True` as "this combatant's anchor" has the same bug latent in it. v2.49.51 fixed `_drop_caster_concentration`. v2.49.53 fixed the 🔁 log. v2.49.54 fixes the swap loop. The remaining sites: `_concentration_buff_for` (used by `_maybe_concentration_save`) — also has the bug latent but a paired-condition victim taking damage and rolling a "CON save" for someone else's concentration spell is an edge case worth filing separately. Tracked in the Filed section below.
**Description (cont 2):** Why a victim shouldn't be able to "drop" the paired condition by casting their own concentration spell. The Hold Person caster is the one sustaining the spell via their own concentration; what happens to THE VICTIM's concentration doesn't end the source caster's spell. The victim can't unilaterally end someone else's spell by casting their own — only the source caster's actions (damage taken → failed CON save, voluntary end, incapacitation, death) end Hold Person. If the victim could end the paired buff by casting their own concentration spell, that'd be a major gameplay break.
**Description (cont 3):** Why a regression guard for own-anchor swap. The source filter narrows the swap-loop drop condition. The risk in narrowing is over-narrowing: if the filter accidentally protected own anchors too, casting a new concentration spell wouldn't replace the old one — broken RAW one-at-a-time. The regression test pre-seeds Magnus with `concentration-bless` (source=Magnus), casts Hex, and asserts the anchor was DROPPED. Without this test, an over-broad filter (e.g. `if b.get("source_char_id") is not None` without the `!= self` clause) would silently regress all swaps.
**Description (cont 4):** Why this isn't catching a real incident yet. The current demo doesn't have a flow that triggers the bug naturally — to be a Hold Person victim AND cast a new concentration spell, the victim has to first be paralyzed (which incapacitates them, blocking spell casting). Sleep / Suggestion / Calm Emotions are non-incapacitating concentration spells that leave the victim able to cast — but those aren't in the demo. The bug was discovered while writing v2.49.53's harness test setup (which deliberately constructs a paired-buff scenario via `/battle` PUT to bypass the can't-cast-while-paralyzed gate). Filing the fix now keeps the rule semantically correct ahead of future spell additions.
**Description (cont 5):** Verification. Ran `test_paired_buff_preserved_when_caster_swaps` pre-fix: failed (Paralyzed dropped from Magnus's buff list after Hex install). Post-fix: passes (both buffs co-exist). `test_own_anchor_swap_still_works` passed both before and after — the regression guard. Full regression: 245 harness tests pass (was 243, +2 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass. No existing tests touched the bug condition so no surprise breakages.

### Fixed
- `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_install_buff` swap loop — applies the `source_char_id is None or == character_id` filter inside the swap branch. Paired condition buffs from other casters are now preserved when the combatant casts a new concentration spell. Matches the source filter already applied in `_drop_caster_concentration` (v2.49.51) and the 🔁 log emission (v2.49.53).

### Added
- `tests/harness/test_swap_preserves_paired_buffs.py` — 2 tests (paired-buff-preserved / own-anchor-still-replaces).
- `docs/test-harness-coverage.md` — catalog entry; total 243 → 245.

### Notes
- **Backward compat.** Pure behavior fix — no schema, broadcast shape, or response shape change. Existing callers and tests are unaffected (none triggered the bug condition because the demo lacks non-incapacitating concentration-spell-on-victim flows). The fix is forward-compatible with Sleep, Suggestion, Calm Emotions, etc.
- **Source-filter is now the canonical predicate**: `source_char_id is None or == character_id` means "this combatant is concentrating on this buff." Three call sites now use it: `_drop_caster_concentration` (v2.49.51), `_install_buff` 🔁 log (v2.49.53), `_install_buff` swap loop (this commit). If a fourth site emerges, refactor into a helper.

### Filed
- **`_concentration_buff_for` has the same latent bug** — it returns the first `concentration: True` buff on a combatant without checking source. Used by `_maybe_concentration_save` (the CON-save-on-damage path). A paired-condition victim taking damage would roll a save against the DC for their suffered buff, treating it as their own concentration. Out of scope here; filed for a separate audit.
- **Helper-ify the source-filter predicate** — three call sites use the same `src is None or src == character_id` pattern. A `_is_own_concentration_buff(buff, character_id) -> bool` helper would dedupe. Punt unless a fourth site lands.

## [2.49.53] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **🔁 GM audit log when a caster swaps to a new concentration spell.** Closes the swap-replaced-by-new-cast follow-up filed in v2.49.52. The four-emoji concentration audit set is now complete: 💔 failed CON save (v2.39.0) · 💀 incapacitated (v2.49.48 / .49 / .51) · ✋ voluntary /end_buff (v2.49.52) · 🔁 swapped (this commit). Pre-fix, `_install_buff` silently dropped the old concentration anchor via the RAW one-at-a-time rule — the `buff_update` broadcast carried `replaced_concentration` keys but no narrative roll-log entry. A GM scanning the log saw the new spell go up but had no audit trail for what was dropped. Fix captures the (key, name, source_char_id) of each replaced concentration buff DURING the swap loop, then after the existing broadcast + paired-cleanup + 💀 paths run, emits a `type=roll` GM-only entry for each replaced anchor: `note=f"🔁 NAME swapped concentration: OLD → NEW"` and breakdown `f"Concentration swapped — cast NEW"`. The `not incapacitates_target` guard prevents double-logging when v2.49.51's 💀 path is the real RAW cause. Source filter (`old_src is None or old_src == character_id`) scopes the log to anchors the caster actually owned — a paired condition (`concentration: True` but `source_char_id` = enemy caster) doesn't generate a spurious 🔁 even if the (pre-existing, separately-filed) swap-loop bug drops it. 3 new harness tests pin the happy-path + a paired-buff negative + a fresh-install negative. PATCH — additive log; broadcast shape and `/cast_*` response shape unchanged.
**Description:** Two edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_install_buff` — added a parallel list `replaced_concentration_meta: list[tuple[str, str, object]]` capturing `(key, name, source_char_id)` for each buff dropped by the existing swap loop. After the v2.49.51 💀 emission block (so the 💀 takes precedence on the incapacitation path), emit a `type=roll` GM-only event per replaced anchor when `is_concentration AND replaced_concentration_meta AND not incapacitates_target`, filtered to entries where `old_src is None or old_src == character_id`. **(2)** `tests/harness/test_swap_concentration_log.py` (NEW, 3 tests). Test strategy uses `/battle` PUT to pre-seed a concentration buff on the caster's combatant — the demo doesn't expose two different concentration-spell endpoints for any single PC (Hex is Warlock-only, Hunter's Mark is Ranger-only, save-or-suck concentration spells aren't all on one spell list), so seeding is the cleanest way to exercise the swap path with a known-different key.
**Description (cont):** Why filter by `source_char_id` on the REPLACED buffs. The swap loop's pre-v2.49.53 behavior — `if is_concentration and b.get("concentration"): replaced_concentration_keys.append(b_key); continue` — looks at the concentration flag without checking who's actually concentrating. If Magnus is a Hold Person victim (carrying Paralyzed flagged `concentration: True` with `source_char_id` = enemy caster) AND Magnus casts Hex, the swap loop wrongly treats Paralyzed as Magnus's anchor and drops it. That's a separate bug (filed below). The 🔁 log's source filter prevents the bug from producing misleading audit entries — even though the buff was dropped, Magnus wasn't actually concentrating on it, so "Magnus swapped concentration: Paralyzed → Hex" would be wrong narrative.
**Description (cont 2):** Why `not incapacitates_target` is the right guard rather than `not replaced_concentration_keys.intersection(preexisting_own_anchors)`. When Tavik Hold-Persons Magnus, the RAW cause is incapacitation — the v2.49.51 path emits 💀 for Magnus's lost Hex. The swap loop ALSO drops Hex (because Paralyzed is `concentration: True`). Pre-v2.49.53 these were silent; with both paths emitting logs, we'd get DOUBLE entries: one 💀 ("Magnus lost concentration on Hex — incapacitated (Paralyzed)") plus one 🔁 ("Magnus swapped concentration: Hex → Paralyzed"). The 💀 names the actual RAW reason; the 🔁 names a mechanical side-effect. Skipping 🔁 when `incapacitates_target` is True keeps the log cleaner — one event, one log entry.
**Description (cont 3):** Test approach: `/battle` PUT pre-seeding. The seed inserts a buff dict directly into Magnus's combatant `buffs` array; subsequent `/cast_hex` runs `_install_buff` which sees the seeded buff in `target.get("buffs")` and processes it through the swap loop. This bypasses the spell-casting validation (slot consumption, class check, etc.) for the seeded buff while still exercising the install path under test. Three scenarios:
  1. Own-anchor swap (positive): seeded buff has `source_char_id` = Magnus → 🔁 fires, log names "concentration-bless → Hex."
  2. Paired-buff swap (negative): seeded buff has `source_char_id` = 99999 (an enemy marker) → swap loop still drops it (bug) but 🔁 log does NOT fire — that's the source filter doing its job.
  3. Fresh install (negative): no seeded buff → swap loop has nothing to replace; no 🔁 log.
**Description (cont 4):** Verification. Ran the new tests pre-fix: all 3 failed (no 🔁 broadcast). Post-fix: all 3 pass. Full regression: 243 harness tests pass (was 240, +3 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass.

### Added

### Notes

### Filed
- **Swap loop wrongly drops paired conditions** — the existing replacement loop at `_install_buff` line ~436 drops every `concentration: True` buff on the combatant when a new concentration buff lands, regardless of whether the combatant actually owned the dropped buff. A Hold Person victim with `Paralyzed` (concentration=True, source=enemy) who casts Hex would lose the Paralyzed buff via this bug. The visible outcome (Paralyzed disappears) might even seem correct in some readings, but RAW the source caster's Hold Person is independent and shouldn't end. Fix: extend the replacement filter to only drop buffs with `source_char_id is None or == character_id`. Out of scope for v2.49.53 (which only filters the LOG); filed for a separate fix that mirrors the source-aware filter at the swap-loop level.

## [2.49.51] - 2026-05-21

**Schema version:** 56
**Commit summary:** **RAW: incapacitating a concentrating PC now drops THEIR concentration, with a 💀 GM log naming the cause.** Closes the non-damage incapacitation gap filed in v2.49.49. PHB p.203: "you also lose concentration on a spell if you are incapacitated or killed." Pre-fix, when an enemy caster Hold-Personed a Hex'd PC, the visible OUTCOME was correct (Hex dropped) — but only because the existing concentration-swap logic in `_install_buff` accidentally produced it: Paralyzed has `concentration: True`, so it "replaced" Hex via the one-concentration-at-a-time rule. The cause was wrong (the PC isn't choosing to concentrate on Paralyzed; they're suffering it) and there was no audit log to explain the drop. Fix makes the incapacitation drop explicit + load-bearing: a new `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS` frozenset enumerates the RAW-incapacitating condition keys (paralyzed / incapacitated / stunned / petrified / unconscious / asleep). When `_install_buff` lands one of these on a target, it snapshots the target's OWN concentration anchors BEFORE the replacement loop, lets the existing replacement run, then emits a 💀 GM-only log per anchor naming the incapacitating buff. If the incapacitating buff itself is `concentration: False` (e.g. future Sleep impl), the anchor is also explicitly removed via `_remove_buff` so the fix isn't dependent on the swap-by-concentration heuristic. `_drop_caster_concentration` is refined to filter by `source_char_id` so paired condition buffs from other casters aren't swept when the helper fires (death-save callers also benefit — dead PC drops only their own anchors, not paired conditions another caster is concentrating on them with). 3 new harness tests pin the new behavior + a regression guard for the v2.38.0 paired-cleanup path. PATCH — bug fix + log addition; reuses existing broadcast shapes.
**Description:** Three edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py` — new `_INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS = frozenset({"paralyzed", "incapacitated", "stunned", "petrified", "unconscious", "asleep"})` constant near `_SPELL_CONDITION_MAP`. Charmed and Frightened deliberately excluded — those conditions constrain action choice but don't incapacitate per RAW. **(2)** `_install_buff` — before the existing replacement loop, computes `incapacitates_target = key in _INCAPACITATING_BUFF_KEYS and (src_of_new is None or src_of_new != character_id)` (the second clause skips the bizarre self-cast-Hideous-Laughter edge case), then snapshots `preexisting_own_anchors` (concentration-flagged buffs where `source_char_id` is None or == character_id — i.e. anchors the target is concentrating on, not paired conditions from other casters). After the existing replacement + paired-cleanup runs, if `incapacitates_target` AND `preexisting_own_anchors` is non-empty: for each anchor, (a) if it's still in `new_list` (incapacitating buff wasn't concentration=True so the swap didn't remove it), call `_remove_buff` to drop it cleanly; (b) emit a `type=roll` GM-only log with note `f"💀 {caster_name} lost concentration on {anchor_name}"` and breakdown `f"Concentration ends — incapacitated ({buff_label})"`. **(3)** `_drop_caster_concentration` — added `source_char_id` filter (`src is not None and src != character_id` → skip). Necessary so the helper doesn't sweep paired conditions when called by a death-save handler on a victim of someone else's Hold Person. **(4)** `tests/harness/test_incapacitation_drops_concentration.py` (NEW, 3 tests).
**Description (cont):** Why the fix works through `_install_buff` rather than a higher-level hook in `cast_spell`. `_install_buff` is the chokepoint every PC-targeting buff install routes through (PC-failed-save resolution at line 6564, direct PC buff installs at lines 10090/10434/10672, etc.). Hooking here means a future Sleep / Stunning Strike / Power Word Stun endpoint that lands an incapacitating condition gets the RAW drop for free. The NPC path (`_install_buff_on_combatant_id`, line 512) is NOT hooked because NPCs don't track their own concentration anchors in our current implementation — adding the helper there is filed for the NPC-concentration follow-up if/when that lands.
**Description (cont 2):** Why both the "existing replacement already handles it" AND the new hook need to coexist. The existing replacement (line 411: `if is_concentration and b.get("concentration")`) drops Hex when Paralyzed lands because BOTH are flagged concentration. This is right outcome / wrong cause: the swap rule treats the victim as "switching" concentration spells, when RAW says they're losing it because they're incapacitated. Three reasons to add the explicit hook even though the visible outcome currently matches:
  1. **Log emission**. The swap path emits no GM log; the player sees the buff disappear but the GM has no audit entry. The new 💀 log names the cause.
  2. **Non-concentration incapacitation**. The day someone adds Sleep (RAW: target falls Unconscious, NOT a concentration spell), the swap rule wouldn't fire (different flags). The explicit `_remove_buff` call covers it.
  3. **Semantic correctness**. The reason field in the log carries "incapacitated (Paralyzed)" not "concentration swap." A future telemetry consumer can filter on the right cause.
**Description (cont 3):** Why `_drop_caster_concentration` needed the source filter. Before the v2.49.51 change, the helper scanned every `concentration: True` buff on the target combatant. If a PC was a victim of someone else's Hold Person (carrying a Paralyzed buff with source_char_id=enemy), AND the PC also had a concentration anchor of their own (e.g. they were Hexing someone before getting paralyzed), AND the PC died — the death-save handler called `_drop_caster_concentration` which would have scanned the victim's buff list and tried to drop BOTH their Hex anchor AND the Paralyzed buff sourced by the other caster. Dropping Paralyzed from the victim is wrong: the source caster is still concentrating on it; the paralyzed-on-victim should only drop when the source caster's concentration ends. The new filter `src is None or src == character_id` keeps the helper scoped to anchors the target owns. Existing callers (roll_death_save, override_death_save) keep working because anchors have source_char_id=None (Hex) or src=self (concentration-spell-slug anchor from save-or-suck PC-fail path).

Gracefully no-ops if the seeded spell index doesn't expose Charm Person. `test_source_caster_concentration_still_cascades` guards against the source-filter regressing the v2.38.0 paired-cleanup: Tavik Hold-Persons Magnus, then Tavik manually ends his own concentration → Magnus's Paralyzed should still drop via the existing cascade.
**Description (cont 5):** Verification. Ran `test_paralyzed_pc_drops_own_concentration` pre-fix (just the filter, no explicit log emission): test passed on the visible state (Hex dropped via swap) but the 💀 log assertion failed (no log emitted). Post-fix: all 3 pass. Full regression: 237 harness tests pass (was 234, +3 new); 33 encounter-sim tests still pass. Also caught a pre-existing flake in `test_roll_3_failures_emits_skull_log` (v2.49.50) — the test exhausted Magnus's Warlock slots when the loop ran 15 iterations in a suite-order context that had used Magnus earlier; added a `long_rest` inside the retry loop. The 0-HP case was the most misleading: the save was still rolled (may have been a nat-20), but the log claimed it "failed." **Description:** Two file edits + one new test file. **(1)** `app/routes/tabletop_routes.py::_drop_caster_concentration` — accepts a new keyword-only ``reason: str = "incapacitated"`` param. Before calling `_remove_buff`, snapshots each concentration buff's key + name + paired-buff list (the cleanup helper mutates state in place, so reading after-the-fact returns empty paired lists). After successful removal, emits a `type=roll` GM-only log entry: `note=f"💀 {caster_name} lost concentration on {buff_name}{paired_note}"` + `breakdown=f"Concentration ends — {reason}"`.
